newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to compensate Airtel for phone licensing fee.
newsitem.headline: Spain to compensate Airtel for phone licensing fee.

text.p: Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado said on Wednesday that Spain was in talks to compensate Airtel, the nation's second mobile telephone operator, for its original licensing fee of 85 billion pesetas.
"The European Commission told us to return the fee or take compensatory steps," Arias Salgado told journalists.
Arias Salgado said the talks with Telefonica de Espana, which was the monopoly mobile phone operator in Spain before the second license was awarded, and Airtel were advanced.
Arias Salgado said that a deal could provide special prices or conditions for the connection of Airtel to Telefonica's network.
He added that within the context of the deal the size of Telefonica's investment in mobile phones would be discounted from the 85 billion pesetas.

Telefonica, currently in the midst of the sale of the state's final 20.9 percent stake in the telecommunications group, earlier reported net earnings rose 20.1 percent in 1996. (( --Madrid Newsroom +34 1 585 2167))
